To find the standard deviation of the random variable $Z = 2X - Y$, we first determine its variance, $\text{Var}(Z)$.

The formula for the variance of a linear combination of two random variables $X$ and $Y$ is:
$$\text{Var}(aX + bY) = a^2\text{Var}(X) + b^2\text{Var}(Y) + 2ab\text{Cov}(X, Y)$$

In this case, $a = 2$ and $b = -1$. Thus:
$$\text{Var}(Z) = \text{Var}(2X - Y) = (2)^2\text{Var}(X) + (-1)^2\text{Var}(Y) + 2(2)(-1)\text{Cov}(X, Y)$$
$$\text{Var}(Z) = 4\text{Var}(X) + \text{Var}(Y) - 4\text{Cov}(X, Y)$$

We are given the standard deviations $\sigma_X = 3$ and $\sigma_Y = 4$, so:
$$\text{Var}(X) = \sigma_X^2 = 3^2 = 9$$
$$\text{Var}(Y) = \sigma_Y^2 = 4^2 = 16$$

The covariance is related to the correlation coefficient $\rho_{XY}$ by:
$$\text{Cov}(X, Y) = \rho_{XY} \cdot \sigma_X \cdot \sigma_Y$$
Given $\rho_{XY} = -0.5$, we have:
$$\text{Cov}(X, Y) = (-0.5) \cdot 3 \cdot 4 = -6$$

Now substitute these values back into the variance equation for $Z$:
$$\text{Var}(Z) = 4(9) + 16 - 4(-6)$$
$$\text{Var}(Z) = 36 + 16 + 24$$
$$\text{Var}(Z) = 76$$

The standard deviation $\sigma_Z$ is the positive square root of the variance:
$$\sigma_Z = \sqrt{76} \approx 8.717797887$$
